title: Apology and technical summary for partner integrations — 2027-04-07
body:
Audience: Customers with partner integrations (webhooks, external routing, and third-party connectors)

Summary and apology
We are writing to apologize for the disruption some customers experienced between 2027-04-06 21:10 UTC and 2027-04-07 02:48 UTC that affected requests routed through partner integrations (notably webhooks and some third-party connector flows). We know this caused errors and delayed or failed responses for production traffic; we are deeply sorry for the impact and inconvenience.

What happened (plain-language overview)
- At ~2027-04-06 21:10 UTC an internal routing component began incorrectly classifying certain partner-originated requests as a background/low-priority traffic class.
- Misclassification caused those requests to be batched differently and routed to a compatibility path that was overloaded under the concurrent workload, producing elevated error rates (5xx) and timeouts for affected integrations.
- Automatic fallback rules that normally reroute to an alternate capacity pool did not trigger due to a configuration regression introduced during a rollout the previous day.

Scope and customer impact
- Affected customers: a subset of customers using partner-provided connectors and webhook-based integrations; approximately 2.3% of total Redwood API requests in the window were impacted.
- Symptoms observed by customers: increased 500/502 errors on webhook delivery attempts, elevated webhook retry rates from third-party vendors, delayed responses for integrations that rely on synchronous callbacks.
- Data integrity: No user-generated content was modified or lost within Redwood. Messages that were successfully acknowledged by Redwood remained intact. Some webhook deliveries were retried by third parties; we are coordinating with affected partners to reconcile duplicates where they occurred.

High-level timeline (UTC)
- 2027-04-06 20:55 — Canary rollout of routing change started (engineering rollout).
- 2027-04-06 21:10 — First error signals from partner-routing metrics (increased error-rate, elevated latency).
- 2027-04-06 21:18 — On-call SRE paged and investigation begun. Initial hypothesis: batching/regression in routing decision logic.
- 2027-04-06 21:45 — Scoped rollback attempted for the canary; rollback did not fully disable the misclassification due to a deployment orchestration bug.
- 2027-04-06 22:30 — Engineering created mitigation to force all partner-originated traffic to the stable routing path; partial recovery observed.
- 2027-04-07 00:10 — Full rollback of the routing change completed and validated.
- 2027-04-07 02:48 — Monitoring confirmed error rates returned to baseline and remaining queues drained.

Immediate mitigations and current status
- We disabled the rollout change and forced partner-originated requests onto the stable routing path.
- We adjusted retry and backpressure settings for the compatibility path to reduce cascading failures.
- We added a temporary rule to surface partner-originated request anomalies to the incident dashboard and notify SRE automatically.
- Current status: service operating normally; no ongoing errors related to this event as of 2027-04-10.

Root cause (summary)
- The root cause was a combination of: (1) a configuration regression in the routing decision logic introduced during a canary rollout, and (2) a deployment orchestration bug that prevented a partial rollback from fully reverting the misclassification rule.
- The misclassification caused traffic to shift into a compatibility execution path that had not been exercised at production scale with the recent code changes. That path saturated, producing timeouts and 5xx responses.

Customer-facing remediation and next steps (what we are doing to prevent recurrence)
1) Fix deployment orchestration regression — Engineering has implemented an immediate patch to the rollout controller to ensure rollbacks revert all dependent configuration keys. This patch is in canary and will be promoted to all regions after validation (completion ETA: 2027-04-14).
2) Hardening routing decision tests — We are adding integration tests that specifically simulate partner-originated traffic classes at scale to catch misclassification regressions earlier (ETA for test coverage: 2027-04-21).
3) Expand automatic fallbacks — We will update fallback rules so that if a compatibility path exceeds a defined saturation threshold, traffic is automatically diverted to the stable pool without requiring manual intervention (ETA: 2027-05-05).
4) Monitoring & alerts — New anomaly detection rules for partner routing flows have been added to the production dashboards; we will publish an abbreviated view for customers via a public status page widget to improve transparency (ETA: 2027-04-20).
5) Partner coordination playbook — Customer Success and Platform will publish a short runbook for common partner vendors describing retry idempotency, duplicate handling, and reconciliation steps to reduce friction in future incidents (ETA: 2027-04-18).

Guidance for affected customers (practical steps)
- If you observed duplicate webhook deliveries from your vendor during 2027-04-06 21:10 to 2027-04-07 02:48 UTC, first check your application’s idempotency logic. Where duplicates were stored, please follow your normal de-duplication procedures.
- If you need a CSV of requests routed during the incident window for reconciliation with partners, contact customer-success@redwood.ai with the subject line "Request: routing-reconciliation CSV — INC-842" and include your account ID. We will prioritize these requests.
- If your integration uses synchronous callbacks, consider configuring a short client-side deduplication window or idempotency key when possible; our team can share templates for common partner vendors.

Data integrity statement
- We have confirmed that there was no unauthorized data modification or deletion within Redwood as a result of this event. The issue affected routing and delivery of requests, not storage. Any partial or failed deliveries were at the connector/webhook layer external to Redwood.

Compensation and SLA credits
- If you were impacted and have an SLA contract, we will evaluate outage minutes for SLA credit eligibility. To request an SLA credit review, open a support ticket referencing INCIDENT-842 and your account contract number. Customer Success will expedite reviews for verified impact.

Who to contact
- Primary CSM contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) — for account-specific reconciliation and follow-up.
- Technical liaison: Liam O'Connor (liam@redwood.ai) — for integration-level technical questions.
- Incident artifacts: status page incident record (https://redwood.statuspage.io/incidents/INC-2027-042) and postmortem (internal link provided above).

Planned external follow-ups
- Short follow-up note (this doc) will be posted to customers listed on the incident contact list within 72 hours.
- Detailed customer-facing postmortem (final) with attachments (CSV of affected request IDs on customer request, synthesized timeline, and remediation verification) will be published within 30 days.

Draft note to copy onto status page (concise, public-friendly)
We experienced elevated error rates for a subset of partner integrations between 2027-04-06 21:10 UTC and 2027-04-07 02:48 UTC due to a routing configuration regression during a rollout. The issue has been resolved; service is operating normally. We are preparing a customer-facing postmortem and steps we are taking to prevent recurrence. If you were impacted, please contact customer-success@redwood.ai and reference INCIDENT-842.

Internal reviewer checklist (for Customer Success / SRE / Product)
- [ ] Confirm final root cause language with engineering (done).
- [ ] Validate CSV export process for affected request IDs (SRE).
- [ ] Approve public status page wording and schedule the postmortem publication (product owner).
- [ ] Confirm partner outreach list and assign owners (CS manager).

Status of this draft
- Version: 0.9 (customer-facing draft).
- Target audience: impacted customers, partners, and account teams.
- Next update: incorporate feedback from engineering and legal, finalize public wording, and publish to status page and direct customer contacts by 2027-04-13.

Acknowledgement
We know customers rely on Redwood for predictable inference flows and tight integration behavior. We are committed to learning from this incident, improving our rollout safety, and working closely with affected customers and partners to reduce friction.

-- Aisha Patel, Customer Success Lead
